copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Qatar and Switzerland together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Qatar side, by +11.3pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, Switzerland comes in 190 points ahead — Qatar at 1640, Switzerland at 1830. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Qatar to win at 20%, the draw at 19%, and Switzerland to win at 61%. The home side reads 20% on this distribution — the model's central case for Qatar.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Qatar to win at 9%, the draw at 15%, and Switzerland to win at 76%. Polymarket has Qatar at 9%, which prices out at American odds of +993; the model has the same side at 20%. The +11.3pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Qatar, that haircut lands the model at 15%; the market is at 9%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +5.7pp. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Qatar priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 22 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: The +11.3pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Qatar side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Qatar side still clears the Pick threshold.
copy.summary: The model thinks Qatar are mispriced. Our number reads 20% on the home side; the market reads 9%. The +11.3pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Qatar v Switzerland · the model leans Qatar
